title: Galactic Face-off
caption: The interacting galaxies NGC 454, imaged by the Dark Energy Camera on the Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope
celestial: NGC 454 · constellation Phoenix · about 160 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys/LBNL/DOE & KPNO/CTIO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA · Image processing: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage/NSF NOIRLab), J. Miller (Gemini Observatory/NSF NOIRLab), M. Rodriguez (Gemini Observatory/NSF NOIRLab) & M. Zamani (NSF NOIRLab)

recognition.text: NOIRLab Image of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Two galaxies face off in the constellation Phoenix, with a red elliptical galaxy called NGC 454 E at the top and NGC 454 W, a blue, gas-rich irregular galaxy, below it. Together they are known as NGC 454, about 160 million light-years away, and their encounter spans a hundred thousand light-years.

Although their interaction is at an early stage, both galaxies are already badly distorted. Material from each has been stretched far beyond its main body, from scattered stars at the top right to globular clusters forming at the lower left of NGC 454 W. Dust lanes cross NGC 454 E, while NGC 454 W barely resembles the disk galaxy it was thought to be.

A faint, veil-like halo surrounds the pair, and many young stars populate the system, further evidence of an early merger. The two are now gravitationally bound and will eventually combine into one galaxy.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (11.98 x 6.74 arcminutes) and distance (160 million light years), the frame spans roughly 558,000 × 314,000 light-years. Its light set out about 160 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Taken with DECam on the Blanco 4-meter Telescope through g, r and z filters. The colour mapping isn't published.
